paper_metadata.title: Research on the thermal stability of a near α titanium alloy before and after laser shock peening

evidence.quote: The room-temperature tensile properties and thermal stability of Ti834 alloy before and after laser shock peening (LSP) were investigated.
The experimental material used in the present work was produced by the Northwest Institute for Nonferrous Metal Research. After multiple forging, a bar with a diameter of 150 mm was obtained.

mechanisms.name: dislocation pinning by α2 phase
mechanisms.material_state: exposed at 600 °C for 100 h in air

evidence.quote: Previous reports pointed out that the α2 phase is a brittle phase which can pin the movement of the dislocations during the deformation [19,20]. This is one of the reasons that the ductility of the alloy decreases sharply after thermal exposure.

mechanisms.name: oxygen embrittlement of α-case
mechanisms.material_state: LSP-treated then exposed at 600 °C for 100 h in air

evidence.quote: This brittle α-case easily cracks during long-term exposure due to the enormous oxygen solubility of the Ti lattice which is distorted by interstitially dissolved oxygen generating considerable stresses[25].

mechanisms.name: oxygen diffusion along defects
mechanisms.material_state: LSP-treated then exposed at 600 °C for 100 h in air

evidence.quote: For the laser shock peened Ti834 alloy, defects such as the dislocations were formed near the surface of specimens during the plastic deformation. These defects can serve as the passage way for the diffusion of oxygen during the exposure, thus more α-case formation near the surface of the specimens.
